name: Core World
desc: You grew up in the heart of what remains of civilization. Vast data-nets, towering arcologies, and complex social hierarchies define life here. Air filtered, water pure, dangers hidden behind polite smiles and corporate logos. You know how to work the system: which bureaucrat to charm, which archive code unlocks restricted tech. Your social networks are your lifeline — powerful and demanding, but essential to surviving the maze.

feature.name: Institutional Leverage
feature.text: The Core Worlds run on bureaucracy and influence. When you are working those systems — getting a permit, accessing a restricted file, working a social event — you may roll your Duality Dice. On a success (10+), you gain 1 Favor Token. You can spend Favor Tokens to automatically succeed on similar institutional tasks later, no roll required. If you are a Diplomat, you begin each session with 1 extra Favor Token.

name: Trade Hub
desc: You were raised in the chaotic symphony of a bazaar. The air smells of spices, ozone, and the quiet desperation of those with nothing left to trade. Your market intuition sniffs out profit or disaster a parsec away. Your information networks are gossip, shipping manifests, the whispers of black-market dealers. You learned young that knowing what's about to happen is worth more than owning what's already happening.

feature.name: Market Oracle
feature.text: You know how to read the currents of trade. When negotiating prices or seeking information about goods, you can gamble resources on rumors. Roll Comprehend (DC 12). On a success, you gain a piece of true, actionable information and 1 Hope. On a Critical Success, you learn a secret that grants you Advantage on related rolls for 24 hours. On a failure, you have spent the resource on a bad rumor and gain nothing, but the Keeper may use the failed attempt as a story hook.

name: Frontier Colony
desc: Your home was grit, rust, and shared hardship. Neighbors would share their last water ration without a second thought. Practical ingenuity is your creed. Can you MacGyver a comms array from a broken toaster and some solar cells? Of course. Bonds run deep, but so do obligations. If you owe Old Man Jax a favor on Persephone's Reach, you pay it. The frontier teaches that the only insurance against the next disaster is the people who survived the last one.

feature.name: Scrap-Savvy Ingenuity
feature.text: You can improvise tools and simple devices from junk. When you do, roll your Fear die to determine the effect. On a low roll (1-3), the device works for one use, then breaks spectacularly. On a higher roll (4+), it works reliably for the scene. Once per long rest, you can reroll this Fear die if you sacrifice a personal item of sentimental value to the project — a memento welded into the chassis, a family ring sacrificed for its conductive metal.

name: Void Station
desc: You grew up in a pressurized can hurtling through nothing. Claustrophobic? Maybe. But you breathed recycled air alongside a dozen species. Technical adaptation is instinct — you feel when the oxygen scrubbers are unhappy by their hum. Cultural fluency is a second language: trade insults with a Kryllian miner at dawn, sip tea with a Celestiari diplomat by afternoon. Void Station natives understand every other being is just trying to get through the day.

feature.name: Cross-Species Intuition
feature.text: Your upbringing has made you adept at understanding different perspectives. You begin each session with 3 Linguistic Tokens. You can spend 1 token to reroll a Hope die on a negotiation check. You can spend 1 token to treat your Fear die as a Hope die for a single negotiation roll. You regain all spent tokens by mediating a faction dispute or after a long rest.

name: Free Fleet
tag: Family Found in the Deep Black
desc: Home is not a place. It is the next jump. Stellar navigation is in your bones. You navigate pulsar fields like others walk city streets. Fleet solidarity is your creed. That scar on your shoulder matches your crewmate's. You find family not in blood but in shared experience of the deep black. Free Fleet natives know your crew is your tribe, ships are alive in ways planets cannot be, and the best people are those who learned to live in motion.

feature.name: Voidborn Kinship
feature.text: You share a deep bond with your fellow travelers. When recalling information about stellar hazards or aiding allies from your fleet (defined as any crew you have traveled with for more than a tenday), you may reroll a single failed piloting check. Alternatively, you can let an ally in your system use your Hope die result as their own for one roll, transferring your moment of fortune into their hands.

name: AgriSynth
desc: You were born beneath the soft, pulsing glow of nutrient lamps. Your first breath was air scrubbed by great AgriSynth processors. The rhythm of life was set by the silent, omnipresent Harvest-Minds — vast AI networks managing every aspect of food production. You understand biology as someone who grew up watching it managed by intelligent systems: pattern, cycle, intervention, harvest. You know when a field is healthy and when something is wrong.

feature.name: Nourished by Nature
feature.text: Your sterile but life-focused upbringing gave you a unique understanding of biology. You have Advantage on Knowledge checks to stabilize creatures near death. You also have Advantage on Survival checks to find or purify food and water, but only in technologically-supported environments (stations, ships, settled worlds with infrastructure). On a wild planet without automation, your training does not translate cleanly.

name: The Displaced Enclave
desc: You grew up in one of the hidden Ailuran enclaves — stations, asteroid warrens, or camouflaged surface settlements that existed in the margins for longer than most civilizations have records. Your childhood was vertical: narrow towers, deep shafts, climbing routes, the sound of claws on metal as the heartbeat of daily life. Privacy was sacred. Then the Veil Rip dissolved your cloaking, and the galaxy saw you. Yours chose to step forward.
restriction: Ailuran-specific. A non-Ailuran character cannot select Displaced Enclave; the cultural specifics do not translate. Ailurans may also select any of the other six communities.

feature.name: Ghost Protocol
feature.text: You were raised in a culture that elevated concealment to an art form. Once per session, you can declare that you have already prepared an escape route, hidden a cache of supplies, or established a fallback position in your current location, even if you did not explicitly state this earlier. The Keeper sets specifics (must be plausible). If your class is Scout or has reconnaissance training, the preparation includes one additional useful detail.
